source.title: Reward Scale Robustness for Proximal Policy Optimization via DreamerV3 Tricks
source.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36); arXiv:2310.17805

confidence_rationale: This is the deliberate counterweight in the pull and the most decision-relevant entry for calibrating what a probe-K result will mean. It is the only paper found that directly tests whether DreamerV3's normalisation machinery TRANSFERS to a different algorithm, which is exactly the inferential step MECH-459 makes when it imports Hafner's prescription into REE's model-free raw-view actor-critic. The finding is explicitly negative on the general question -- the tricks 'do not transfer as general improvements to PPO' across more than 10,000 compute-hours of experiments -- while positive on a narrower one: PPO with the tricks performs comparably to PPO WITH reward clipping and significantly outperforms PPO WITHOUT reward clipping. Peer-reviewed at a top venue with a large compute budget, so source quality is high and the null is well-powered rather than an underpowered miss. Confidence 0.71 reflects solid quality and clear relevance, discounted because the paper tests DreamerV3's normaliser as a BUNDLE on dense-reward Atari, so it cannot isolate the specific sparse-reward, near-zero-return regime in which MECH-459 locates REE's pathology.
failure_signatures: Normalisation machinery that is load-bearing in one algorithm can fail to produce any general improvement when transplanted into another, even at very large compute budgets.
The measured benefit of DreamerV3-style normalisation in PPO was substitutive rather than additive -- it recovered what reward clipping already provided rather than adding gains on top of it.
Evaluating a bundle of tricks jointly cannot attribute effect to any single component, so a bundle-level null does not license a component-level null.

mapping.source_claim_statement: DreamerV3's tricks (symlog, percentile return normalisation, twohot distributional critic) do not transfer as general improvements to PPO. Across >10,000 compute-hours, PPO with these tricks performs comparably to PPO with reward clipping, and significantly outperforms PPO without reward clipping.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-459 imports Hafner's prescription across an algorithm boundary, from DreamerV3's imagination-based actor-critic into REE's model-free raw-view actor-critic. Sullivan et al. performed the equivalent import into PPO and got a general null. This directly weakens the prior that installing a floored one-sided percentile normaliser in place of REE's (adv - mean)/(std + 1e-8) will move the foraging floor, and correspondingly it raises the prior that probe K returns a null. The narrower positive result is the more useful part for REE: the tricks mattered specifically where an unbounded reward scale would otherwise have destabilised training -- i.e. the benefit was about magnitude robustness, which is precisely the axis MECH-459 argues REE's stacked normalisers have already destroyed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries. (1) REGIME MISMATCH, and it cuts BOTH ways: their evaluation is dominated by dense-reward Atari, whereas MECH-459's pathology is specific to sparse/zero-forage episodes where the advantage vector is near-zero -- so this null does not directly test REE's regime, and a probe-K positive would not contradict it. (2) BUNDLE CONFOUND: symlog, percentile normalisation and the twohot critic were evaluated together, so no component-level attribution is possible; a bundle-level null cannot be read as evidence against the percentile normaliser specifically. (3) DIRECTION OF THE REE TEST IS OPPOSITE: they ADDED tricks to a working baseline, whereas probe K REMOVES a suspected-harmful operator from a floored baseline. Adding a corrective to a healthy system and removing a pathology from a broken one are not the same experiment, and a null on the former is weak evidence about the latter.
mapping.source_context: Model-free deep RL; PPO on Atari (Arcade Learning Environment) plus additional benchmarks; >10,000 GPU-hours; simulation only, no biological data.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: peer-reviewed at NeurIPS, unusually large compute budget, and a published negative result (which carries extra credibility given publication bias against nulls). Mapping fidelity moderate -- right inferential question (does the DreamerV3 normaliser transfer across algorithms?) but wrong reward regime and bundled components. Transfer risk is the highest in this pull because the dense-reward Atari setting is where MECH-459 would itself predict no effect, so the null may be regime-explained rather than mechanism-refuting.
